A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same CoordTok study. Their main text, figures, tables, equations and complete appendices are readable and support reliable matching across relocations and renumbering.

before.justification: V3 reports original UCF-101 video reconstruction, unconditional generation and ablation results, including supplementary quantitative and qualitative results.

after.justification: V4 retains those original results and adds baseline evaluations, computational analysis and fine-tuning measurements.

M1.justification: The architecture, losses and training stages remain unchanged, but the reported interpolation-index rule changes from floor(i(H'-1)) to floor(iH'), with analogous changes for the other axes. This changes neighbor selection as written; the PDFs do not establish whether the implementation changed.

E1.justification: Both evaluate UCF-101 video reconstruction and unconditional generation at 128x128 resolution. The added 16-frame rFVD evaluation uses subclips of the existing 128-frame videos. CosmosTokenizer's different pretraining is a comparator qualification, not a new dataset experiment for CoordTok.

E2.justification: V4 substantially broadens comparisons: OmniTokenizer-DV, OmniTokenizer-CV and CosmosTokenizer-CV join reconstruction Table 1; OmniTokenizer-CV also joins Figures 1a and 4. Latte-L/2 joins generation-quality and efficiency Tables 2 and 3. The earlier comparators remain.

E3.justification: V4 adds training-FLOPs measurement and a 16-frame rFVD protocol using the retained 10,000 evaluation videos. Appendix E reports 80,000 subclips but inconsistently states that each 128-frame video produces 16 non-overlapping 16-frame subclips. The main training budgets, splits and evaluation protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D adds targeted analyses of computational scaling with video length (Figure 9) and reconstruction before versus after the existing LPIPS fine-tuning phase (Table 9). Earlier sampling, model-size, triplane-size, dynamics, frequency and token-count analyses are retained; the qualitative examples are relocated.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. Existing Pearson-correlation analyses are unchanged, and the new results continue the same point-estimate reporting practice.

E6.justification: Table 1 gains substantial baseline and low-token results. Tables 2–3 add Latte-L/2 results: FVD 1901.8, 21.4 seconds and 3.1 GB. New figures and Table 9 report FLOPs, 16-frame rFVD and pre-fine-tuning outcomes. Retained CoordTok scores are unchanged. Table 9 gives pre-fine-tuning rFVD 186.3, whereas its accompanying prose says 188.3.

T1.justification: Most decoder mathematics moves from v3 Appendix A.1 into v4 Section 2.2. However, scaling coordinates by H'-1, W'-1 and T'-1 before flooring changes to scaling by H', W' and T'. This is a non-equivalent indexing definition, not merely new notation. No new theorem or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction and conclusion retain the same contributions: scalable coordinate-based video tokenization, 128-frame encoding with 1280 tokens, and memory-efficient generation of long videos. Additional comparisons do not redefine these claims.

C2.justification: V4 explicitly identifies the fine-tuning tradeoff: improved rFVD and LPIPS accompany worse PSNR and SSIM, refining v3's general statement that fine-tuning improves reconstruction quality. It also qualifies CosmosTokenizer comparisons because of different pretraining. Existing dynamic-video limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: Appendix C adds OmniTokenizer architecture, loss and input/token-shape details, plus Latte's attention design. Core hyperparameters and Tables 5–6 remain unchanged. Most decoder details are relocated, although v3's explicit explanation of applying coordinate-matched positional embeddings before decoder layers is omitted while positional embeddings remain listed architecturally.

R1.justification: V4 adds Cosmos and Latte references and discusses them as comparators. OmniTokenizer was already cited in v3 but now receives substantive baseline discussion. The related-work taxonomy and central novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: Section 2.2 is reorganized into input/target, representation and reconstruction explanations, largely incorporating existing appendix material. Appendices D–F regroup analyses, quantitative results and qualitative examples. Most other prose remains stable, with limited wording and acknowledgement edits.

P2.justification: The central reconstruction table is substantially rebuilt with token-type classification, separate token-budget blocks and an rFVD column. Figures 1a and 4 gain comparator displays; Figures 9–10 and Table 9 are added. Qualitative displays are reorganized, including moving v3 Figure 6 to v4 Figure 12, while retaining their examples.

improvement.justification: Broader baseline comparisons and new FLOPs and fine-tuning analyses better support the efficiency argument and clarify reconstruction tradeoffs compared with v3. These provide a limited net gain, tempered by the unexplained interpolation-index revision, inconsistent subclip counts and Table 9's 186.3 versus 188.3 reporting discrepancy.
